How to squat with good form.

This doesn't specifically mention it but to help build the form, go face/toes up against a wall to keep your knees from going too far forward.

I also go until my thighs hit my calves, basically ass to floor.

I'm currently doing the 5x5 routine. It's more full body and less isolation so it works those unknown muscles that help stabilize/transition between movements. I really like it.

Edit: Forgot a few tips. Go down slow to really try and feel what muscles you are working, to make little adjustments. If it's not stimulating the right muscles, adjust. Everyone is physically different so it's not a one form fits all. Plus keep the weight on your heels not your toes and the bar on your shoulder blades not your neck. That becomes more important with the heavier weights. My friend can do a squat with a empty bar balanced on his shoulders with no hands... It's impressive and insulting and I hate them for it haha
